latest_release.name: v0.2.6
latest_release.body:
### Changed

- `string_match`: replaced recursive glob matching with iterative backtracking; bitwise `|` on the character comparison avoids a short-circuit branch.

---

## Install

**Linux (x86_64)**
```bash
curl -Lo zedis https://github.com/barddoo/zedis/releases/download/v0.2.6/zedis-v0.2.6-linux-x86_64
chmod +x zedis && sudo mv zedis /usr/local/bin/
```

**Linux (ARM64)**
```bash
curl -Lo zedis https://github.com/barddoo/zedis/releases/download/v0.2.6/zedis-v0.2.6-linux-aarch64
chmod +x zedis && sudo mv zedis /usr/local/bin/
```

### Verify checksums

```bash
curl -LO https://github.com/barddoo/zedis/releases/download/v0.2.6/SHA256SUMS
curl -LO https://github.com/barddoo/zedis/releases/download/v0.2.6/zedis-v0.2.6-linux-x86_64
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing
```

## Quick start

```bash
# Start server (listens on 127.0.0.1:6379 by default)
zedis

# Connect
redis-cli ping
# PONG

SET hello world
GET hello
# "world"
```

detail.readme: # Zedis [![Release](https://github.com/barddoo/zedis/actions/workflows/release.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/barddoo/zedis/actions/workflows/release.yml) A Redis-compatible in-memory data store written in [Zig](https://ziglang.org/), designed for learning and experimentation. Zedis implements the core Redis protocol and data structures with a focus on simplicity, performance, and thread safety. ## Features - **Redis Protocol Compatibility**: Supports the Redis Serialization Protocol (RESP), including pipelined commands. - **Multiple Data Types**: Strings and integers, lists, time series, and Bloom filters. - **Core Commands**: Key management (`DEL`, `EXISTS`, `TYPE`, `TTL`, `EXPIRE`, `KEYS`), strings, lists (`LPUSH`/`RPUSH`/`LRANGE`, ...), and `RANDOMKEY`. - **High Performance**: Written in Zig, with a single-executor command path and no global store lock. - **Key Expiration**: Lazy TTL expiry on access, plus expiry checks during eviction. - **Disk persistence (RDB)**: Point-in-time snapshots of your dataset, loaded at startup when `appendonly` is off. - **Append-only file (AOF)**: Durable write-ahead logging with group commit. - **Memory Budgeting**: Redis-compatible `maxmemory` with eviction, `-OOM` rejection for allocating commands, and cgroup-aware auto-sizing inside containers. - **Pub/Sub**: Decoupled communication between services, with push delivery to idle subscribers. - **TLS**: Optional TLS 1.3 listener (ztls/AWS-LC) with certificate/key/CA configuration and optional mutual TLS via `tls-auth-clients`. - **Observability**: Real `INFO` counters (connections, ops/sec, hit rate, memory, AOF state), `SLOWLOG`, `LATENCY`, and a `METRICS` command exposing Prometheus text exposition. - **Graceful shutdown**: `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` and `SHUTDOWN [NOSAVE|SAVE]` stop accepting, drain clients, flush the AOF, and close the listeners. `CONFIG REWRITE` persists runtime changes. - **Time Series**: Time series data structure. **Now with Gorilla compression!** - **Opinionated Design**: No multiple logical databases, expiry is lazy only. ## Caveats - Zedis is intentionally single-store. It does not support multiple logical databases and does not expose Redis `SELECT`. It adds complexity and segment memory. This follows the reasoning Salvatore Sanfilippo gave when he called Redis multiple databases one of [his worst design decisions](https://groups.google.com/g/redis-db/c/vS5wX8X4Cjg/m/8ounBXitG4sJ). ## Quick Start Download the binary from the [releases page](https://github.com/barddoo/zedis/releases) or build from source to get started with Zedis. ### Prerequisites - [Zig](https://ziglang.org/download/) 0.17.1 (pinned in `build.zig.zon`) - `make` and a C compiler: `zig build` compiles LuaJIT from `vendor/luajit` ### Building and Running ```bash # Clone the repository with its submodules git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/barddoo/zedis.git cd zedis # Build the project (optimized, ReleaseFast) zig build --release=fast # Run the server zig build run --release=fast ``` The server will start on `127.0.0.1:6379` by default. ### Testing with Redis CLI You can test Zedis using the standard `redis-cli` or any Redis client: ```bash # Connect to Zedis redis-cli -h 127.0.0.1 -p 6379 # Try some commands 127.0.0.1:6379> SET mykey "Hello, Zedis!" OK 127.0.0.1:6379> GET mykey "Hello, Zedis!" 127.0.0.1:6379> INCR counter (integer) 1 127.0.0.1:6379> TYPE mykey string ``` ### TLS Enable the TLS listener in the config file (see `zedis.conf` for all options): ```conf port 0 # optional: serve TLS only tls-port 6380 tls-cert-file /etc/zedis/server.crt tls-key-file /etc/zedis/server.key tls-ca-cert-file /etc/zedis/ca.crt tls-auth-clients no # yes (default), no, or optional ``` Then connect with any TLS-capable Redis client, for example: ```bash redis-cli --tls --insecure -p 6380 ``` ## Docker Pre-built images are available on [Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/r/barddoo/zedis): ```bash docker run -p 6379:6379 barddoo/zedis ``` ### Variants | Tag | Base | Notes | Use case | | ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------- | -------------------------- | | `latest`, `x.x.x`, `x.x.x-debian`, `x.x.x-slim` | Debian Trixie slim | Larger, glibc base | Default; broader ecosystem | | `x.x.x-alpine`, `alpine` | Alpine 3.20 | Smallest with shell | Size-sensitive deployments | | `x.x.x-distroless` | Distroless static | No shell | Security-sensitive | ### Persistent data Mount a volume to persist data across restarts: ```bash docker run -p 6379:6379 -v zedis-data:/var/lib/zedis/data barddoo/zedis ``` ### Custom config ```bash docker run -p 6379:6379 -v ./zedis.conf:/etc/zedis/zedis.conf barddoo/zedis ``` ## Development ### Project Structure The codebase is split by responsibility: - `src/app/` — server lifecycle, client connections, config, clock - `src/storage/` — store, KV allocator, lists, time series, Bloom filters, search - `src/commands/` — command handlers and registry - `src/persistence/` — AOF and RDB - `src/protocol/` — RESP parser and serializer - `src/util/` — mailbox, stack writer, types, compression - `src/benchmarks/` — micro/load benchmarks See `docs/server-architecture.md` for the current server thread model and request flow. ### Memory Management See `docs/memory-architecture.md` for the current allocator layout, memory budgets, and runtime allocation behavior. See `docs/store-cache-layout.md` for the store's hash-table layout and cache behavior. ### Building for Development TLS is provided by [ztls](https://github.com/lalinsky/ztls), which builds and links AWS-LC from source, so no system TLS library is needed. The native ztls engine speaks TLS 1.3; `tls-protocols` accepts `TLSv1.3` and `TLSv1.2`, but TLS 1.2 is not negotiated. LuaJIT is built from the `vendor/luajit` git submodule, so clone with `git clone --recurse-submodules`, or run `git submodule update --init --recursive` before building. ```bash # Build in debug mode (default) zig build # Build optimized release (ReleaseFast; use this for benchmarks and performance testing) zig build --release=fast # `--release` with no mode also picks ReleaseFast (the preferred mode in build.zig) zig build --release # Run the full test suite zig build test # Run a focused subset zig build test -Dtest-filter="Store" # Format the source zig fmt . ``` ## AI Disclaimer This project was developed with some AI help. Most of the code was written by hand. ## Contributing Contributors are welcome! Whether you're fixing bugs, adding features, improving documentation, or suggesting enhancements, your contributions are appreciated. Feel free to: - Open an issue to report bugs or suggest features - Submit pull requests with improvements - Share feedback and ideas Check out the [open issues](https://github.com/barddoo/zedis/issues) to see where you can help. ## Stay Connected - Subscribe to my [newsletter](https://charlesfonseca.substack.com) ## Thanks - [Andrew Kelley](https://andrewkelley.me) - For creating the amazing [Zig Language](https://ziglang.org/). - [Redis](https://redis.io/) - For the inspiration and protocol design. - [TigerBeetle](https://tigerbeetle.com/) - For the memory management and the tiger style. - [Karl Seguin](https://github.com/karlseguin) - For the great articles.
